A design system
built for humans and agents.

Flavor DS is delivered over MCP. Any project — new or existing — imports it, and the system adapts: tokens, themes, components, and accessibility guarantees included.

Import via MCP Explore Core UI

1152 themes, one file

16 hues × 3 saturations × light/dark × AA/AAA — every combination resolves from nine attributes on <html>. No theme forks, ever.

Contrast is computed, not promised

Every text and surface pairing ships with its WCAG ratio calculated to two decimals. Pairings outside the approved list are not expressible in the semantic tier.

Agents are first-class users

The MCP server exposes tokens, themes, components, and adaptation logic as tools. An agent asks flavor_adapt_project and gets stack-specific adoption steps.

Density, direction, elevation

Three density modes rescale every control. RTL flips every layout via logical properties. Dark mode elevations get lighter as they rise — not a naive inversion.

Canvas

Review the whole system on one board

Canvas — the EthiGov review board, ported byte-for-byte via the canvas-maker skill — renders every page of this site as live device frames on an infinite, pannable board: the real app, not screenshots. Pin a comment on any element; adjust type, colour, spacing and radius from this system's real tokens only (with an explicit detach for one-offs); switch any theme axis or edit a token and watch every frame restyle at once. The board itself wears the brand theme and follows light and dark with the frames — it is built from the tokens it reviews. Feedback is written to .canvas/feedback.json in the repo so it travels with the branch, and Copy feedback exports a block an agent can apply unambiguously — the same block the MCP serves as flavor_canvas_feedback.

Agent Ready

A memory, not a manual

The whole system is indexed at build time — 86 chunks with priorities and tags — and flavor_recall hands an agent the twelve global rules first, then only what the task in front of it needs, under a token budget, with everything it left out listed by id. Deterministic, tested in CI, and the same code runs live on the page.

How agents read Flavor llms.txt 
flavor_recall({ task: "build a login form" })

# Global rules            ← always, first
1. Semantic tokens only …
# Contract                ← building UI
Theme axes · Adopt Flavor
# Relevant to the task    ← ranked, budgeted
Text input   score 9.1
Sign in template  8.4
Button       7.6 …
# Also available          ← omitted, by id
component-checkbox-radio, template-settings …
